questions.question: COCOMO-II estimation model is based on

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.14; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: COCOMO II is an algorithmic cost estimation model that uses mathematical formulas derived from empirical regression analysis of historical project metrics to predict effort and schedule.

questions.question: Cost estimation for a project may include

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.15; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: The answer includes software cost, hardware cost, and personnel costs; these are all relevant components of a project cost estimate.
questions.explanation_ar: التكلفة الكلية تجمع تكاليف البرمجيات والعتاد والأفراد.

questions.question: In COCOMO model, if project size is typically 2 - 50 KLOC, then which mode is to be selected?

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.16; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: In COCOMO, the Organic mode represents relatively small software projects (typically 2 to 50 KLOC) developed by experienced teams working in familiar, stable in-house environments with relaxed requirements.
questions.question_ar: في نموذج COCOMO، إذا كان حجم المشروع عادة بين 2 و50 KLOC، فأي نمط يختار؟
questions.explanation_ar: النمط organic يناسب المشاريع الصغيرة والمتوسطة بهذا المدى.

questions.question: COCOMO-II was developed at

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.17; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: COCOMO II was developed by Barry Boehm and his research team at the Center for Software Engineering (CSE) at the University of Southern California (USC) during the 1990s.
questions.explanation_ar: COCOMO-II طور في جامعة Southern California.

questions.question: Which one is not a Category of COCOMO-II?

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.18; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: COCOMO II identifies four target project categories / application sectors: End-User Programming, Application Generators & Composition Aids, System Integration, and Infrastructure Sector. "Requirement Sector" does not exist in COCOMO II taxonomy.
questions.question_ar: أي مما يلي ليس فئة من فئات COCOMO-II؟
questions.explanation_ar: requirement sector ليست من فئات COCOMO-II المعتمدة.

questions.question: Which one is not an infrastructure software?

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.19; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: Infrastructure software provides core foundational services and platforms upon which application software runs; examples include Operating Systems, DBMS, Compilers, Network protocols, and Device Drivers. "Result management system" is an end-user application, not infrastructure software.
questions.question_ar: أي مما يلي ليس من برمجيات البنية التحتية؟
questions.explanation_ar: نظام إدارة النتائج تطبيق وليس برمجية بنية تحتية.

questions.question: How many stages are in COCOMO-II?

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.20; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: COCOMO II provides three increasingly detailed estimation stages tailored to the life cycle: Stage 1 (Application Composition Model), Stage 2 (Early Design Model), and Stage 3 (Post-Architecture Model).

questions.question: Which one is not a stage of COCOMO-II?

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.21; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: The three official stages of COCOMO II are Application Composition, Early Design, and Post-Architecture. "Comprehensive cost estimation model" is an invented distractor.
questions.question_ar: أي مما يلي ليس مرحلة من مراحل COCOMO-II؟
questions.explanation_ar: نموذج التكلفة الشامل ليس مرحلة من مراحل COCOMO-II.

questions.question: In Putnam resource allocation model, Rayleigh curve is modeled by the equation

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.22; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: In the Putnam resource allocation model, manpower utilization rate $m(t)$ over time follows Norden's Rayleigh curve equation: $m(t) = 2 K a t \cdot e^{-at^2}$, where $K$ is total life-cycle effort, $a = \frac{1}{2 t_d^2}$, and $t$ is elapsed project time.
questions.question_ar: في نموذج Putnam لتخصيص الموارد، يمثل منحنى Rayleigh بالمعادلة:
questions.explanation_ar: منحنى Rayleigh في نموذج Putnam يأخذ الصيغة 2Kat e^-at^2.

questions.question: In Putnam resource allocation model, technology factor 'C' is defined as

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.23; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: Putnam's Software Equation relates product size $S$ to total effort $K$ and development time $t_d$ by $S = C \cdot K^{1/3} \cdot t_d^{4/3}$. Solving algebraically for the technology factor $C$ yields $C = S \cdot K^{-1/3} \cdot t_d^{-4/3}$.
questions.question_ar: في نموذج Putnam، عامل التقنية C يعرف بأنه:
questions.explanation_ar: عامل التقنية يعبر عن العلاقة بين الحجم وزمن التطوير.

questions.question: Risk management activities are divided in

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.24; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: Risk management activities are divided into two fundamental primary categories: Risk Assessment (identification, analysis, prioritization) and Risk Control (planning, resolution, monitoring).
questions.explanation_ar: إدارة المخاطر تنقسم إلى تقييم المخاطر وضبط المخاطر.

questions.question: Which one is not a risk management activity?

source.reference: Aggarwal & Singh, Software Engineering (3rd ed.), MCQ 4.25; publisher key p. 498

note.ar: قوبل السؤال مع مفتاح الناشر المطبوع.
note.en: Checked against the printed publisher key.

questions.explanation: The established activities of software risk management are Risk Assessment (evaluating exposure) and Risk Control (mitigating and monitoring risk). "Risk generation" is not one of the two listed management activities.
questions.question_ar: أي مما يلي ليس نشاطاً من أنشطة إدارة المخاطر؟
questions.explanation_ar: توليد المخاطر ليس نشاطاً معتمداً في إدارة المخاطر.
